name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.31.0 — the render gate lands: mock↔component fidelity is judged at the render, not at the pixel (ADR-0002, specs/20260824/01). Three new scripts, all dependency-free: `render-inventory.browser.js` is a bare in-page expression the host's capture command evaluates, returning an accessibility-tree-shaped inventory of **painted** text (computed `text-transform` applied — DOM text differs from paint on correct code), `aria-label` kept as a separate `name` facet so a label glyph never collides with a real control, roles, page-coordinate boxes, and the `srOnly`/`fixed`/`outOfFlow`/`dataPositioned` flags; `render-compare.js` matches two inventories by LCS over in-flow painted text and reports `text-missing`/`text-extra`/`order`/`role`/`positioning`/`geometry` findings under script-constant tolerances (dx 1%, dw 1%, dh 15% — the measured zero-false-positive floors), with `dyRel` computed into `--json` but never a finding (unbound-region height poisons it) and static-control→link auto-excused behind one printed `📌 Auto-picked` veto line; `render-gate.js` drives the host's declared `design.render.capture` command across the `design/targets.json` theme × viewport matrix, serving the host's `design/` directory itself over Node's built-in `http` on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port so mock-relative `../tokens.css` resolves, binding each mock state to a story id through `.claude/design-coverage.json` claims (`stories`), and honouring a `ready`/`boot` lifecycle that kills only the process it started. Exclusions are structural, never tolerances: `aria-hidden`/`data-contract="none"` subtrees never enter the inventory, absolutely-positioned entries are matched by presence but excluded from ORDER, and fixed/sticky, sr-only, or `data-positioned` entries are excluded from GEOMETRY — each one a measured false-positive class. Exit alphabet 0 pass / 1 findings / 2 precondition / 3 capture-or-readiness failure, so a capture failure can never read as green. No pixel layer exists and the capture contract deliberately has no screenshot output, so no host can wire one back in as a "quick advisory". `spec.config.json` gains the `design.render` block (`capture`, `url`, optional `ready`, `boot`, `readyTimeout`) — a grounding-contract change, so every host's `/spec:doctor` will report stale grounding until it declares the key or refreshes. `/spec:review` runs the gate as an advisory evidence leg on designed specs where `design.render` is declared, and prints one skip line naming the key where it is not; it is never a `verdict.js` leg. 7.30.0 — replay attributes red legs against the originating review's own recorded baseline instead of treating every red leg as mutation evidence, closing a censoring/false-due-window-reset defect measured 2026-08-23 on ~27% of selectable CLEAN closes (specs/20260823/09): `--select` derives the baseline from the selected row's own `legs` array (red = `exit !== 0`, `smoke` exit 4 exempt) with zero extra leg runs, appending `baselineRed=<legs>|none|unknown` and `baselineLegs=<legs>|unknown` after the existing five selection tokens; `spec-review-driver.js`'s `parseSelection` captures both when present (absent → `null`, never a parse failure) and prints them in the REPLAY step body. replay.md's Phase 1 step 7 re-keys the retry/leg-caught path to newly-red legs only: a red leg is explained when it's in `baselineRed` or is `reconcile` (deterministic exemption — the mutation is File-Plan-confined by step 4's worker contract, so reconcile redness, definitionally out-of-plan, can never be mutation-caused); an unattributable red leg routes to one `AskUserQuestion` whose dismissal records `unresolved`. `--record --legs` gains `baseline-red:<leg>[,<leg>]`, valid for `caught`/`missed`/`unresolved` alongside `green`; `unresolved` also keeps a `red:<leg>` arm for a step-7 dismissal, which requires `--patch` and now refuses `--workflow` (the reviewer never ran); `leg-caught` keeps `red:<leg>` for newly-red-only. Historical ledger rows, including the motivating `rp_1b176ebff5c7` misrecord, are never rewritten; `--stats` is unchanged. Deviation: D8 named 7.29.0 as the bump target, but that version was already at HEAD by build time (a concurrent session in this repo won the race) — per this repo's own next-free-version Gotcha this lands at 7.30.0 instead, recorded in the spec's deviations sidecar. 7.29.0 — a derived session queue closes the 2026-08-18-style "reconstruct the ordering by hand" session (specs/20260823/08): `spec-queue.json`, one file in the git common directory (`git -C <root> rev-parse --git-common-dir`, a relative result resolved against `<root>`; shared by every linked worktree, invisible to `git status`), stores JJ's intended work order across briefs plus free-text prompt items and their done-when predicates (closed vocabulary D5: `brief-state`, `spec-exists`, `ledger-count` with a `baseline` stamp, `manual`). New `spec-queue.js` (subcommands `next add bump defer done list ok hello`, exposed as `/spec:queue`) owns every write: reconcile-on-invocation (D6) inserts an on-disk brief missing from the queue right after its `Depends on:`/letter-suffix parent with an `auto_placed` stamp that only `bump`/`defer`/`done`/`ok` clears, and seeding (D7 — absent/empty file, an explicit write subcommand only, never the hook) fills all non-done briefs in roadmap order with zero stamps and one summary line. `spec-status.js` stays the sole `--next` derivation surface (D2 — every live consumer shells its stdout verbatim, and the one `--json` consumer, autopilot, was deleted 2026-08-18): the queue is a read-only overlay inside `deriveNext()` — queue position orders unblocked entries across briefs, deliberately overriding cross-brief closest-to-done ranking; prompt items surface verbatim with no `@path` suffix; `/spec:escape` red-observation entries keep rank −3 supremacy over every queue position (D10); a linked worktree suppresses the overlay entirely (D9 — the global pointer misleads mid-spec). No queue file means `--next` is byte-identical to today (D1–D3). A new SessionStart hook (matcher `startup|resume|clear` — D8 deliberately excludes `compact`/`fork`, mid-task refresh not a fresh session) runs a thin bash guard (`session-queue.sh`, zero node-startup cost when no queue file exists) that prints the top item's paste line plus one veto notice per un-cleared `auto_placed` item in the main checkout, or a finish-this-tree line inside a linked worktree; an empty queue with no notices prints nothing. New `/spec:status` anomaly kinds `queue-auto-placed` (names the veto command) and `queue-orphan` (a queued brief with no matching file) join the existing anomaly narration. Deviation: D12 named 7.28.0 as the bump target, but a concurrent same-day incident fix had already claimed it at HEAD by build time — per this repo's own next-free-version Gotcha this lands at 7.29.0 instead, recorded in the spec's deviations sidecar.
